versions.content:
# MC-110 Media relations (rev. 2026-02)

1. Media line: the on-call PR specialist answers reporters within 30 minutes, 24/7. Acknowledge, get the deadline,
   and find the right source.
2. Spokespeople: PR designates physician and staff spokespeople. Executives (CEO, CNO, VPs) speak only with the VP
   of Marketing and Communications' agreement.
3. Nothing is off the record. Do not speculate, and do not comment on personnel matters.
4. Patients (HIPAA, 45 CFR 164.510): if a reporter asks for a patient by name and the patient has not opted out of
   the facility directory, you may give a one-word condition (undetermined, good, fair, serious, critical) after
   checking with the house supervisor. Do not confirm or deny anything about a patient asked about without a
   name, or about a patient who opted out ("no information" status), even to say they are not a patient. Never
   confirm a patient's presence or care in connection with a complaint, claim or lawsuit; refer to the approved
   statement. A family's public statements do not change this.
5. Personnel: do not confirm leave, discipline or employment actions for any employee.
6. Embargoes: embargoed material goes only to reporters who agreed to the embargo in writing in advance. An outlet
   that breaks an embargo is excluded from embargoed material for 12 months.
7. Claims, lawsuits and complaints about care: statements are drafted by PR and approved by Legal and the Privacy
   Officer, then the VP. Patient Relations, not PR, contacts patients and families about complaints.
8. Filming or photographing patients requires the patient's prior written authorization (form MC-7), even with
   faces blurred.
9. Labor relations: statements about the nurses' union or the contract are approved by the VP and Labor
   Relations.

# Kessler gift announcement: plan (Doug Brenner, rev. 10/30)

What: the Kessler Family Foundation's $20 million gift, the largest in PBH's history, toward the Kessler
Children's Behavioral Health Hospital, a 48-bed psychiatric hospital for children and adolescents on the
Prairie Bend Medical Center campus. With a $12 million state grant (Gov. Hartley attending).
When: Thursday, Nov. 5, 10:00 a.m. CT, atrium of Prairie Bend Medical Center. Embargo lifts 10:00 a.m. CT.
Speakers: Dr. Ellison (CEO), Gov. Hartley, Ruth Kessler, a patient family (the Garcias, MC-7 signed).
Embargoed briefings (after written agreement): The Prairie Ledger (Dana Corcoran), KPRB (Kim Halsey), Prairie
Business Journal (Victor Pollard), AP (Nate Okoye). Briefings Tue-Wed. NC9 is excluded from embargoes until
Dec. 1 (broke the June embargo). Election Day is Tuesday; no pitching Tuesday or Wednesday mornings.
Approvals: release (Doug, Celeste, Hannah); donor quote (Ruth Kessler); Governor's quote and the grant language
(Jamal Ortiz); CEO remarks (Celeste).
Social: Priya schedules posts in Sprout for 10:00 a.m. CT.
Materials: release, media advisory (Tue), CEO remarks, Q&A, fact board, b-roll.

# EMBARGOED UNTIL 10 A.M. CT THURSDAY, NOV. 5, 2026 (draft v3)

## Kessler family gives $20 million toward children's behavioral health hospital

LINCOLN, Neb. -- The Kessler Family Foundation has given $20 million to Prairie Bend Health toward a $62 million,
48-bed psychiatric hospital for children and adolescents, the largest gift in the system's 110-year history.

The Kessler Children's Behavioral Health Hospital will be built on the Prairie Bend Medical Center campus and is
expected to open in 2029. Funding includes the Kessler gift, a $12 million grant from the state, $26 million
from PBH and $4 million from other donors.

"[Donor quote: pending Ruth Kessler]"

"[Governor quote: pending Office of the Governor]"

"Nebraska families wait too long, and travel too far, for psychiatric care for their children," said Dr. Raymond
Ellison, PBH president and CEO. "This gift changes that."

Today, children who need inpatient psychiatric care in southeast Nebraska are often sent out of state; PBH has
no pediatric psychiatric beds.

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Q&A for Dr. Ellison and Hannah Voss (v2, 10/29)

Q: How much will it cost? A: $62 million; the Kessler gift, a state grant, PBH funds and other donors.
Q: When will it open? A: 2029.
Q: How will you staff it when you can't staff the ER? A: Our nursing vacancy rate is 9% (June), better than the
national average; we'll recruit and train specialized staff starting in 2027.
Q: Why children's behavioral health? A: Demand has doubled since 2019; families travel out of state.
[No questions yet on: current ER concerns, the nurses' contract]

# PBH Heart and Vascular, Hickman (fact sheet for media, approved 10/20)

- Address: 410 Locust St., Hickman. Opened Monday, Oct. 26, 2026.
- Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m. By referral; no walk-ins. Phone 402-555-0320.
- Services: general cardiology clinic visits, echocardiograms, stress tests, cardiac rehab referrals.
- Physicians: two cardiologists rotate from Prairie Bend Medical Center; one nurse practitioner on site daily.
- Spokesperson: Tasha Greer (Marketing) coordinates photos; media requests to the media line.
